dracula.name: Count Dracula
dracula.role: ancient Transylvanian noble and predatory biological monopoly invading London via real estate and maritime loopholes

jonathan.name: Jonathan Harker
jonathan.role: earnest young English solicitor's clerk who discovers Dracula's true nature and audits the vampire's movements

mina.name: Mina Harker
mina.role: schoolmistress and analytical mastermind whose cross-indexed dossiers, shorthand, and reverse hypnosis dismantle Dracula

helsing.name: Abraham Van Helsing
helsing.role: Dutch polymath doctor and philosopher bridging advanced medicine and arcane folklore to coordinate the hunt

seward.name: Dr. John Seward
seward.role: earnest superintendent of the Purfleet lunatic asylum who records patient Renfield and the vampire hunt on wax cylinders

renfield.name: R. M. Renfield
renfield.role: asylum patient whose zoophagous consumption of flies, spiders, and birds mirrors Dracula's metabolic life-absorption

lucy.name: Lucy Westenra
lucy.role: aristocratic debutante whose somnambulism and gradual vampiric infection expose Victorian somatic vulnerability

quincey.name: Quincey Morris
quincey.role: wealthy adventurous American hunter from Texas who finances the expedition and delivers the fatal heart strike

captions.text: and she translates it and types it out.
But she doesn't just type it once.
She types it in manifold.
And we should explain what that means, typing in
manifold. Go ahead. It means using carbon paper to
create multiple identical copies of the document simultaneously.
You strike the typewriter key, it hits the ribbon,
marks the first page, and the pressure transfers the
ink from the carbon paper onto the pages beneath
it. It requires striking the keys with significant physical
force. Yes, she is literally building a
secure redundant database. Data backup.
Data backup. Exactly. And she does the same thing
with Dr. Seard's photograph This is such a cool
detail. Seward is using an Edison wax cylinder
photograph to record his voice.
This was cutting edge technology, but it's locked in
audio format, right? And wax cylinders are fragile.
Furthermore, if you wanted to record over them, you
had to physically shave the wax down, so the
audio is ephemeral. So Mina sits down with the
photograph, puts the tubes in her ears, listens to
Seward's recordings, and types them out.
She transcribes the audio into verifiable text.
She compiles the diaries, the ship's log from the
de meter, the newspaper clippings from Whitby, the letters,
the shipping invoices. She takes all this fragmented
localized data and synthesizes it into a single
cohesive chronological typewritten database.
